Diagnose soft-thresholding power for WGCNA

rna_pick_power.Rd

Evaluates candidate soft-thresholding powers for weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) using normalized expression data stored in an rna_project object. The function filters genes with zero or invalid variance, optionally retains the most variable genes, performs basic expression-data quality control, and evaluates scale-free topology fit across the candidate powers.

Diagnostic plots and a summary of the evaluated powers are provided to support the selection of a suitable soft-thresholding power before network construction.

Usage

rna_pick_power(
  project,
  genes_n = 10000,
  powers = 1:20,
  network_type = c("signed", "unsigned", "signed hybrid"),
  fit_threshold = 0.9,
  plot = TRUE,
  save = TRUE
)

Arguments

project

An rna_project object containing normalized gene expression data and sample metadata.

genes_n

Integer or NULL. Maximum number of genes to retain, selected by decreasing expression variance across samples. Genes with non-finite or zero variance are excluded before selection. If NULL, all eligible genes are retained. Using a subset of the most variable genes can reduce computation time during power evaluation. Defaults to 10000.

powers

Numeric vector of candidate soft-thresholding powers to evaluate. Values must be finite, positive, and unique. Defaults to 1:20.

network_type

Character string specifying the network type used by WGCNA. Supported values are "signed", "unsigned", and "signed hybrid". A signed network preserves the distinction between positive and negative correlations; an unsigned network uses the magnitude of correlations; and a signed hybrid network excludes negative correlations from the adjacency calculation. Defaults to "signed".

fit_threshold

Numeric value between 0 and 1 defining the minimum signed scale-free topology fit index used to flag candidate powers. The signed fit index is calculated from the scale-free topology fit and the sign of its regression slope. Powers meeting or exceeding this threshold are marked in the meets_threshold column of the returned diagnostic table. This threshold does not automatically select a final power or guarantee that the resulting network will be suitable. Defaults to 0.90.

plot

Logical. If TRUE, displays diagnostic plots showing the signed scale-free topology fit across candidate powers and the corresponding mean network connectivity. The horizontal reference line in the fit plot corresponds to fit_threshold. Defaults to TRUE.

save

Logical. If TRUE, attaches the diagnostic result to the project under the analyses slot with subtype "wgcna_power" and invisibly returns the updated project. If FALSE, does not attach the result and instead invisibly returns an object of class power_result. Defaults to TRUE.

Value

If save = TRUE, invisibly returns the updated rna_project object containing the diagnostic result.

If save = FALSE, invisibly returns an object of class power_result, containing the fit diagnostics, candidate powers, network type, fit threshold, numbers of genes and samples used, identifiers of retained genes and samples, identifiers removed during quality control, and the analysis timestamp.

Input data

The expression matrix must be numeric, with genes in rows and samples in columns. Gene identifiers and sample identifiers must be unique. The metadata must identify samples through a Sample column or through its row names. Sample identifiers are matched to the expression matrix column names; metadata must contain an entry for every expression sample.

Expression values must be finite. Genes with non-finite or zero variance are excluded before the most variable genes are selected. WGCNA quality control is then applied to identify and remove additional problematic samples or genes.

Interpretation

The scale-free topology fit and mean connectivity plots provide complementary diagnostics. A higher scale-free topology fit may support a candidate power, but increasing the power can also reduce network connectivity. Therefore, power selection should consider both diagnostics and the biological objectives of the analysis.

The fit_threshold argument defines a diagnostic criterion rather than a universal cutoff. If no candidate power reaches the specified threshold, the function reports this result without automatically relaxing the criterion. Alternative thresholds may be explored when justified by the dataset and the intended analysis.

Scope of the analysis

This function evaluates candidate powers using the samples supplied in the project as a whole. It does not test differential co-expression between experimental groups and does not construct the final network or identify co-expression modules. Group-specific or consensus network analyses require additional steps.

References

Langfelder P, Horvath S. (2008). WGCNA: an R package for weighted correlation network analysis. BMC Bioinformatics, 9, 559. doi:10.1186/1471-2105-9-559
